chunks: My father (rah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ubayd-Allah al-Dahqan from Durust ibn Mansur from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the Miswak, there are twelve virtues: it is from the Sunnah, it cleanses the mouth, it brightens the eyesight, it pleases the Merciful, it whitens the teeth, it removes decay, it strengthens the gums, it makes food appetizing, it removes phlegm, it increases memory, it doubles the good deeds, and the angels rejoice in it.
ai.seo_question: What are the twelve virtues and benefits of using the Miswak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes the Miswak as a comprehensive act of worship that bridges physical hygiene with spiritual elevation. It emphasizes the Prophetic tradition of oral purification, linking tangible health benefits like strengthened gums and improved memory to divine pleasure and the joy of angels, thereby elevating a daily routine into a means of multiplying rewards.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Ahmad b. Idris who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ahmad who said it was narrated to me by Ibrahim b. Ishaq from Muhammad b. Isa from ’Ubayd-Allah al-Dahqan from Durust b. Mansur from Abdillah b. Sinan from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“There are twelve virtues of doing Miswak – it is the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.), it cleans the mouth, improves eyesight, Allah becomes pleased, teeth are cleansed, teeth are prevented from decay, jaws become stronger, it increases appetite, it removes phlegm, it improves memory, it doubles the good deeds of a person and angels become happy.”
